newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Newborn survives 10 hours in Costa Rica outhouse.
newsitem.headline: Newborn survives 10 hours in Costa Rica outhouse.

text.p: A newborn baby in Costa Rica survived 10 hours floating in fecal matter after her mother apparently threw her into the well of an outhouse, police said on Wednesday.
Police spokesman Jose Morales said authorities had not identified the mother.
The incident occurred about 150 miles (240 km) northwest of San Jose in Guanacaste province, a poor region where many communities lack indoor plumbing, Morales said.
The baby girl, who doctors believed was born on Tuesday based on the state of her umbilical cord, was recovering in a hospital, Morales said.
The mother "tied a rock to the baby so it would sink but even so she survived," Morales said, adding the little girl happened to fall in a position that allowed her to continue breathing.
She was discovered by a neighbour who heard wailing.
It is not all that uncommon for poor Central American mothers to ditch their babies into outhouses, presumably because they believe the bodies can decompose without being detected.
A Venezuelan woman travelling in the country was arrested for decapitating her 6-year-old daughter on Sunday, stuffing the remains in plastic bags and throwing them in the garbage.

The Venezuelan woman told police she wanted to "rejuvenate" herself by getting rid of her child. Police said Wednesday they believe the woman had another baby and are investigating whether it too was killed.
